With progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have continued to strengthen. Consistent with the Fed’s 2020 shift to average inflation targeting (Powell, Jackson Hole), the FOMC is keeping the federal funds rate at 0–0.25% and continuing Treasury and agency MBS purchases to allow inflation to moderately exceed 2% for a time, anchoring the average at target. This stance aligns with the New Keynesian policy-rule literature (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler) and the Taylor principle’s emphasis on expectations, while the make-up strategy helps mitigate the classic inflation-bias problem (Barro–Gordon). Implementation via administered rates, including interest on reserves (Goodfriend, 2002), together with forward guidance and QE, supports transmission through the yield curve in line with research on term premia (Cochrane–Piazzesi). Given ongoing pandemic-related supply and demand shocks, the Committee’s risk-management posture remains cautiously accommodative.
